Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a widened mediastinum with an indistinct aortic knob, which is the classic radiographic sign suggestive of traumatic aortic injury (typically at the isthmus) in the setting of blunt trauma. While pediatric patients can have a prominent thymus, the clinical context of a crush accident makes ruling out aortic injury the primary significance of this finding.
